And I noticed my scrubs have been hanging really loose on me lately, even though I'm not trying to lose weight at all. Which is annoying because I just bought these new ones with the extra cargo pockets on the thigh—you really need those pockets for all the tape and extra supplies when you're doing patient transport—and now they just sag right off my waist. turns.doctor_question: With all of this heaviness and the feeling that everything is pointless, have you found yourself having any thoughts that life is not worth living or that you would be better off dead?
turns.patient_response: Well, I haven't... I haven't made any kind of plan to hurt myself or anything like that. But yeah, sometimes I do catch myself just wishing I wouldn't wake up. Like, it would just be so much easier if I could disappear, you know? Just poof, gone. No more dragging myself out of bed, no more dealing with the squeaky transport chairs. It reminds me of this magic show my uncle took me to when I was a kid. This guy, he called himself The Great Zamboni or something, he had this huge cabinet on stage. He put his assistant in there, closed the doors, spun it around, and when he opened it—she was gone. Poof. I always wondered how they did that trick. I mean, I know there's a trap door or mirrors involved. My cousin Eddie tried to explain it to me once. Eddie was always trying to figure out how things worked. He took apart his dad's lawnmower when he was twelve and couldn't put it back together. His dad was furious. They had to pay a guy fifty bucks to come fix it, and fifty bucks was a lot of money back then. Eddie ended up becoming an engineer, though, so I guess taking the lawnmower apart paid off in the end. He lives out in Seattle now. Rains a lot out there. I don't think I could handle all that rain. But yeah, I don't want to kill myself, I just... I just think about how nice it would be to just not be here anymore. Just disappear like that assistant in the cabinet.
